name: Alexander Hamilton Society at Columbia University
description: AHS’s mission is to identify, educate, and launch young men and women into foreign policy and national security careers imbued with the Hamiltonian perspective of strong and principled American leadership in global affairs. At the heart of our approach lies a commitment to vigorous debate and intellectual discourse, while offering programming that is critical to the intellectual and professional development of a new generation of American leaders. name: American Academy of Environmental Engineers and Scientists of Columbia University
American Institute of Chemical Engineers
description: The purpose of this chapter is to promote knowledge of science and engineering and to promote mutual acquaintance and good fellowship among students and between students and instructors, and to provide services when called upon in order to present a good image of the University to the community.

name: Association of Latino Professionals for America Columbia Chapter
description: To empower and develop leaders of character from Latino and other underrepresented communities for the nation in every sector of the global economy

name: Ballet Folklorico Cielito Azul
description: Ballet Folklorico Cielito Azul is Columbia University’s first Ballet Folklorico dance group, dedicated to celebrating and preserving the rich, diverse traditions of Mexico through the artistry of folk dance. Open to all, we welcome anyone passionate about exploring Mexican culture. Through accessible lessons and vibrant performances, we aim to foster a deeper appreciation for Mexican heritage while building a community that honors the beauty and resilience of its traditions.

name: BridgeColumbia
description: We hope to encourage and empower young people to engage in productive civil dialogue on campus and improve the quality of politics.

name: Charles Drew Pre-Medical Society
description: Charles Drew Pre-Medical Society strives to guide, support, and encourage pre-medical students, with a special emphasis on underrepresented students, in their various endeavors to become members of the medical field. We are an inclusive safe space where everyone can feel comfortable expressing themselves without fear of judgment or discrimination.

name: ChicanX Caucus
description: Chicane Caucus is a student organization at Columbia University dedicated to building a supportive community for its members while uplifting the broader Mexican, Mexican-American, Chicane, and Latine community. We work to help students achieve their educational goals, deepen their cultural consciousness, and strengthen their political awareness. Through mentorship, community-building, cultural programming, and advocacy, we aim to foster meaningful connection both within Columbia and beyond it. Our work centers on sharing knowledge, creating opportunities, and contributing to the well-being and

name: Columbia + Barnard Architecture Society
description: Columbia + Barnard Architecture Society is a student-run group providing architectural awareness to undergraduate students at Columbia University and Barnard College. It gives a forum for students interested in architecture as a field of study to ask questions while also learning about graduate schools and the profession within the context of New York City.

name: Columbia Alpha Partners
description: Columbia Alpha Partners (CAP) aims to increase knowledge in investment banking, global capital markets, and real estate, as well as raise awareness of its impact and utilization within and beyond the financial industry. Through instructive seminars, mentoring initiatives, and meetings with successful professionals, CAP provides resources with which members can build greater knowledge of the financial markets and understand the different career paths within finance.

name: Columbia Amarte
description: CU Amarte is a collective that seeks to create accessible and communal artistic opportunities for students on campus, especially those historically excluded from artistic spaces. We emphasize creating art in tandem and building relationships through shared learning and inspiration. Our mission is to empower individuals to express themselves collectively, removing the pressures of perfectionism.

name: Columbia American Society of Mechanical Engineers
Columbia Association for Women in Mathematics
Columbia At Your Service
description: Columbia At Your Service (AYS) is a student-run volunteer program at Terence Cardinal Cooke Health Care Center (TCC), a sub-acute rehab center and skilled nursing facility located on 106th and 5th Ave. Volunteers additionally participate in reflection sessions and spend time volunteering in the Recreation Department at the TCC. AYS is committed to serving TCC residents while also providing opportunities for volunteers to reflect on their experiences in a group-setting and develop as compassionate, thoughtful caretakers.

name: Columbia Ballet Collaborative
description: Columbia Ballet Collaborative (CBC), founded in 2007 by five professional dancers enrolled at Columbia University, is comprised of students from all of the university’s undergraduate colleges and affiliates, some of whom are current or former professional dancers. CBC is student-run and directed and its members have danced professionally with such companies as Complexions Contemporary Ballet, Ballet West, Boston Ballet, Kansas City Ballet, New York City Ballet, Miami City Ballet, North Carolina Dance Theatre, Orlando Ballet, Pennsylvania Ballet, Royal Danish Ballet, The Suzanne Farrell Ballet,

description: We expand access to and promote opportunities for reasoned discussion. Educating and collaborating with other students to develop advocacy skills and public speaking abilities.

Columbia Minecraft Club (CMC)
description: The Minecraft Club started up in June, 2019 after a handful of CU'23 students expressed a common interest in the fantastic game of, well, Minecraft! We established our survival server then, and it was a great way to meet people before our freshman year. We had so much fun playing together, that once we met each other on campus, we started meeting up weekly and decided to make a club for anyone else at Columbia to join. name: Columbia Poker Club
description: Columbia Poker Club brings together poker players for games, workshops, and competitions. Whether you're a beginner or a seasoned pro, you'll find a welcoming community here.

name: Columbia Policy Institute (CPI)
description: The Columbia Policy Institute is a progressive, non-partisan, student-run public policy think tank. As an organization, we strive to create and support solutions-oriented political dialogue and impact policymaking on Columbia’s campus as well as in our community, state, and country. As students, we believe that by harnessing the potential of undergraduates, graduates, professors, and the greater Columbia community we, the members of the Columbia Policy Institute, can start changing the world today.

name: Columbia Public Health Club
description: The CU Public Health Club’s mission is to provide opportunities to engage with Public Health work both on and off campus. Working with Mailman School of Public Health is part of our mission in addition to providing opportunities for education, community work, and awareness of internships and funding through monthly events and online promotion. We recognize that Columbia does not have a pre-professional movement for Public Health and we seek to fill that void.

name: Columbia Queer and Asian (Q&A)
description: We strive to support and empower queer/trans Asian/Asian-American students, while collaborating with queer/POC organizations to create a community and safer space for queer students of color on Columbia's campus and in the greater NYC area. Our main form of communication is through WhatsApp group chat announcements. Join here! https://chat.whatsapp.com/FXFNi0UhHDN1guJjTQE7cO?mode=gi_t

name: Columbia Queer Business Society
description: The Columbia Queer Business Society is dedicated to supporting, uplifting and empowering LGBTQ+ students and allies at Columbia University who are passionate about business, entrepreneurship, and professional advancement. Through mentorship, networking, and advocacy, CQBS seeks to cultivate a vibrant community that fosters excellence, promotes equity, and celebrates diversity.

name: Columbia Raas
description: Columbia Raas (est. 2003) is Columbia University's nationally competitive dance team that celebrates the energy and tradition of the Western Indian dance style, Garba-Raas. Our performances showcase high energy, unique formations, and skillful dandiya maneuvers. We perform at various venues on and off campus, and compete in Garba Raas competitions across the United States. Beyond the dance itself, CU Raas is a group that prides itself on truly being a family.

name: Columbia Sci-Inspire
description: Sci-Inspire is a student-led, volunteer program run by Columbia University undergraduates who provide free, virtual tutoring and mentorship to middle and high school students in the NYC area and beyond. While rooted in STEM, we offer support across a range of subjects and aim to support learners through equitable, student-driven education.

name: Columbia Students for Global Health Equity and Medicine (GHEM)
description: Founded in 2008, GlobeMed at Columbia was one of 46 GlobeMed chapters working to improve the health of people living in poverty around the world. While GlobeMed as an organization has ended, CU GHEM (Columbia Students for Global Health, Equity, and Medicine) lives on to promote public health education within and beyond the Columbia community. It partners with Gulu Women’s Economic Development and Globalization, a human rights organization based in Gulu, Uganda, to provide health services, economic empowerment, psychosocial support and human rights advocacy for the communities surrounding Gulu.

name: Columbia Synapse
description: Columbia Synapse is a student-run organization committed to support, education, and advocacy for the brain injury community. We host weekly virtual support groups where individuals with brain injury and student volunteers come together to share experiences, offer peer support, and discuss challenges navigating life post-injury. We champion student-led advocacy by organizing arts-inspired initiatives, educational programs, and awareness outreach to promote greater recognition of brain injury-related challenges and amplify the voices of the brain injury community. Our goal is to create a lasting

name: Columbia Undergraduate Wealth Management Club
description: The purpose of this organization is twofold: first, to train the next generation of finance leaders interested in Asset/Wealth Management or any tangential sector, and second, to educate undergraduate students about personal finance. As the impending 'Great Wealth Transfer' is set to redefine the financial landscape in the coming decades, our goal is to prepare Columbia’s driven students, who are likely to be future inheritors and business leaders, with the necessary expertise to handle their wealth prudently. Our educational approach connects theoretical learning with practical application, s

name: Columbia University Airplane Club
description: Columbia University Airplane Club provides the unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience designing and manufacturing a RC aircraft as a team. The distinct missions we work on each year push us to solve new problems, collaborate intensively, and learn from both our failures and successes. There is truly no better feeling than watching your creations take flight. That experience motivates us to keep working with the diligence and integrity needed to grow into practical problem-solvers who carry what we learn here into challenges and projects beyond competition.

description: Gourmand is Columbia’s culinary and food-interest group, devoted to creating accessible content, spaces, and events for students to enjoy and learn about food.

name: Columbia University Kidney Disease and Screening Awareness Program
description: CU KDSAP prepares and inspires Columbia undergraduates to enter nephrology while collaborating with Columbia physicians to expand access to kidney disease screening and renal health education in underserved communities.

name: Columbia University Red Cross
description: CU Red Cross is a student organization primarily intended for students interested in public health, the activities of the American Red Cross, and/or other similar topics. The efforts of CU Red Cross, aligned with the aforementioned topics, primarily concern the New York City metropolitan area, the campuses of Columbia University and Barnard College, and the areas surrounding these campuses. name: Columbia University Science Olympiad
description: The purpose of CUSO shall be to promote STEM engagement and outreach among high school students in the tri-state area and beyond through the organization of the Columbia University Science Olympiad Invitational Tournament(s) and the Columbia University Science Olympiad Outreach Program.

Through a community built on education and peer mentorship, CVP equips members with the technical knowledge, professional skills, and the network needed to pursue careers in venture capital and finance. name: Columbia Women's Business Society
description: Columbia Women’s Business Society is an undergraduate femme and/or women’s pre-professional organization at Columbia University devoted to helping undergraduate students of Columbia College, Barnard College, The School of General Studies, and The Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science, advance their pursuit of careers in business through events including, but not limited to, workshops, coffee chats, mentorship initiatives, and career panels. By fostering relationships with professionals in their respective fields, CWBS members gain the support and guidance of businesswomen and

name: Columbia Wushu
description: Columbia Wushu, founded in 2010, is the largest collegiate wushu club in the NYC area. Wushu is a performance-based form of Chinese martial arts that includes barehand and weapon forms, emphasizing strength, flexibility, coordination, and grace. Above all, we prioritize being a welcoming community for students across Columbia’s schools, regardless of experience level.

name: Columbia-Barnard Young Democratic Socialists of America
Columbia-Bronx Oncology Living Daily Program
description: Columbia BOLD arose to bolster the medical system of one of the poorest districts in the U.S.: Bronx, New York. Representing volunteers from across the city, we represent the desire for university students and other volunteers everywhere to diminish the stark inequalities facing cancer patients today.

name: ColumbiAces
description: To provide a welcoming space for aromantic and asexual students and allies. We aim to discuss issues relevant to aromantic and asexual identity and life, providing a space for engagement, education, and building community.

name: Continents: Columbia's Undergraduate Human Rights Magazine
Crowned Lion Innovative Pictures (CLIP)
description: Crowned Lion Innovative Pictures (CLiP) is Columbia University’s undergraduate filmmaker collective dedicated to building a thriving community & a professional development pipeline for student creators pursuing careers in the film, media, and creative industries. CLiP functions as a structured creative network that connects student filmmakers into production teams, and provides members with professional development opportunities, premiere nights, and networking events.

name: CU Boricuas
description: CU Boricuas provides a safe and inclusive space for students who identify as Puerto Rican or strongly advocate for Puerto Rican causes, fostering an appreciation for the culture and engaging in vital social discussions. Moreover, CU Boricuas takes on the role of educating the broader Columbia community about Puerto Rico's intricate history, current affairs, and cultural heritage through academic and recreational activities, while also supporting grassroots non-profit organizations through fundraising initiatives.

name: CU Cities Without Borders
description: CU Cities Without Borders is a student-led collective reimagining how design and justice intersect across cities. Through urban studies, art, research, and community engagement, we explore what it means to decolonize urbanism while helping students engage with urban-facing careers, spatial justice, and the communities that shape city life.

name: CU Model Congress
description: Columbia University Model Congress is a student-run organization that plans and executes one of the largest student-run conferences on campus. Each winter, we bring together hundreds of high school students from across the region for a four-day simulation of the U.S. legislative process.​

name: CU Records
description: CU Records' mission is to strengthen and unite Columbia’s artistic community by providing students with the resources and opportunities to record music and other media. As a recording studio, we train students to become audio engineers equipped to record themselves and others. As a media organization, we promote music and media created in the studio or in association with the club. As a physical studio in a landscape of dispersed digital media, CU Records remains committed to its principle values of collaboration, accessibility, and analog craft. Please consult our website for more information

name: Doctors Without Borders Student Chapter at Columbia University
description: The “Doctors Without Borders” Student Chapter at Columbia University is an interdisciplinary organization dedicated to advocacy and the principles of humanitarian medicine that aims to advance medical ethics and improve access to healthcare.

Gadfly

We publish original essays, artwork, and interviews, with the aim of cultivating philosophical reflection in a variety of media. We also hold weekly discussions and other public events (lectures, film screenings, etc.) with the aim of furthering philosophy beyond the written word. We are deeply committed to the view that philosophy should contribute to—indeed, be a part of—the broader cultural conversation. Thus, we welcome submissions of all forms, on all subjects, by authors both

name: Global Ambassador Program
description: Interested in intercultural exchange? Ready to step out of your comfort zone to make new friends and/or learn new cultures? Thinking of going on study abroad and want more intercultural experiences? GAP is a year-long international friendship program that aims to foster intercultural dialogue among Columbia's diverse student body. The program encourages participation of students from all different backgrounds, cultures, and experiences. GAP provides a brave(r) space for discussing topics influenced by our values. name: Grey Matters CU
description: Grey Matters Columbia University is a literary undergraduate neuroscience journal dedicated to evolving the way we approach, discuss, and research neuroscience and its connections to other areas of study. Neuroscience has an intimidating stigma attached to the field, and our mission is to break down that intellectual barrier to permit the knowledge of neuroscience to be accessible and available to all. We wish for a conversation about neuroscience to happen as casually as a conversation about the newest blockbuster movie.

name: Hearts for the Homeless International at Columbia
Hindu Students Organization
description: The Columbia Hindu Students Organization (HSO) seeks to foster a welcoming and inclusive community where students can connect with and celebrate Hindu culture, traditions, and spirituality. Through events such as Navaratri, Diwali, Holi, weekly bhajans, and other cultural and religious programming, we create opportunities for students to learn, participate, and build meaningful connections with one another. Our mission is to cultivate a vibrant Hindu community at Columbia while sharing the richness and diversity of Hindu traditions with the broader campus community.

name: Hispanic Pre-Law Society
description: The Hispanic Pre-Law Society (HPLS) is on a mission to create and disseminate law resources, information, and professional development experiences for undergraduate Hispanic students. Through mentorship and skill-building opportunities, HPLS seeks to support students in their academic and career pursuits within the legal field.

We perform these songs wherever the kingdom of God may be advanced, but in particular for our peers at Columbia University and the surrounding community. Kappa Alpha Psi® Fraternity, Inc. (ΚΑΨ) is a collegiate Greek-letter fraternity, founded on January 5, 1911 at Indiana University Bloomington. Lincoln Society of Rural Columbia
description: The Lincoln Society at Columbia University exists to support students from rural and small-town backgrounds as they transition to and thrive within Columbia’s academic and urban environment. The organization seeks to create a supportive community, foster mentorship, and promote dialogue around rural identity and representation in higher education.

name: LionHealth
description: The mission of LionHealth is to empower Columbia University undergraduates to design and develop innovative medical technologies that address unmet healthcare needs in underserved communities. name: Mixed Heritage Society
description: The Mixed Heritage Society of Columbia University is a campus organization that seeks to build community amongst students of mixed backgrounds, whether that be through race or ethnicity, mixed religious backgrounds, having parents of two different cultures and/or however else an individual might define their identity in ways that encompasses the notion of being “mixed.”

name: Multicultural Affairs
description: Multicultural Affairs recognizes that affirming each person’s story, encouraging shared responsibility and accountability to shape our community, and nurturing an environment where every student can thrive is critical to our work with students. Our approach through programs, support, and advocacy aims to meet every student at every developmental stage. We serves as a resource for them to capitalize on the rich education and growth found in the active exchange across multiple identities within a community. name: Platypus Marxist Reading Group
description: The Platypus Affiliated Society, established in December 2006, organizes reading groups, public fora, research and journalism focused on the problems and tasks inherited from the "Old" (1920s–30s), "New" (1960s–70s) and post-political (1980s–90s) Left for the possibilities of emancipatory politics today. Read our full Statement of Purpose here: https://platypus1917.org/about/statement-of-purpose/

Postcrypt Coffeehouse
description: Postcrypt Coffeehouse Columbia University's student-run acoustic and folk music venue! Established in 1964, Postcrypt Coffeehouse features professional, amateur, and student performers every Friday and Saturday night of the academic year. Admission is always free and open to the public. Our events feature a diverse array of music and artists; including but not limited to blues, folk, jazz, rock, country, flamenco, bossanova, hip-hop, R&B, rap, and acapella, as well as poetry, comedy, and storytelling. SOL serves as a cultural, social, and advocacy-based organization that uplifts Latine voices at Columbia. It hosts cultural showcases, social events, and community-building initiatives that foster belonging and solidarity. Its goal is to create inclusive spaces that celebrate Latine identities while supporting students academically, socially, and culturally.

name: Student Union for Sustainable Development
description: Welcome to the Student Union for Sustainable Development (SUSD)! We are the main sustainability pre-professional organization built by and for Columbia University undergraduates. SUSD is an organization helping students explore different topics in climate & sustainability to find their niche. We are a central place to connect and amplify Columbia's climate resources.

Tea Club
description: The Columbia University Tea Club is the only student organization at Columbia solely dedicated to highlighting the arts and culture of tea. We are a community of students united by a shared interest in fostering informed dialogue around tea across cultures, traditions, and practices. Throughout the academic year, the club hosts educational and community-oriented events including bi-weekly tea tastings, workshops and demonstrations, guest speaker events, and tea-related socials. name: The Columbia University Journal of Global Health
The Columbia Witness

The community values on which The Crown Magazine was built are Transparency, Journalistic Integrity, and Empathy. These community values will be present in all things related to and published by our organization. Our publication will be the heart of our organization and everything published will exist to uplift, unify, and showcase the beauty of our community. In addition, we hope our publication will create space for dialogue on issues

name: Third Wheel Improv
description: Third Wheel Improv was established in 2013 with the intent to make improv accessible to all students at Columbia University.

Uptown Vocal

Since 1991, "UV" has been cooking up exciting, original arrangements of your favorite jazz standards, pop and rock hits, and more. Uptown Vocal has performed all over: the White House, morning shows, and even the Yankee’s 100th Anniversary Dinner!
